title: How villi soak up food in the small intestine
examples: How does food get into the blood?
Why is the small intestine lined with villi?

levels.label: Small intestine
levels.note: A coiled tube about 6 metres long

explain.say: Digested food has to get from inside your gut into your blood. The small intestine does this, and its secret is an enormous inner surface.

draw.text: How villi soak up food in the small intestine

levels.label: Small intestine
levels.note: A coiled tube about 6 metres long

explain.say: Its inner wall is pleated into folds, and the folds are covered with millions of tiny finger-like bumps called villi, each about a millimetre tall, like the pile on a towel.

levels.label: Small intestine
levels.note: A coiled tube about 6 metres long

explain.say: Zoom in further and every cell on a villus has its own fringe of even tinier bristles, called microvilli. Folds, villi and microvilli together make the surface hundreds of times bigger than a smooth tube.

levels.label: Small intestine
levels.note: A coiled tube about 6 metres long

explain.say: Inside each villus are tiny blood vessels and a lymph vessel called a lacteal. Sugars and amino acids pass into the blood, and fats go into the lacteal, and away they travel.

levels.label: Small intestine
levels.note: A coiled tube about 6 metres long

faq.a: Villi are tiny finger-like bumps, about a millimetre tall, that line the inside of the small intestine. They greatly increase its surface so digested food can be absorbed quickly.
Microvilli are microscopic bristles on the surface of each cell lining the villi. They multiply the absorbing surface even more and carry enzymes that finish digestion.

faq.q: How does food get into the blood?
faq.a: Digested nutrients pass through the cells on the villi into tiny capillaries inside. Sugars and amino acids go into the blood, which takes them first to the liver.
asks: Tell me about blood and lymph in a villus

faq.a: A lacteal is a small lymph vessel in the middle of each villus. Digested fats are packed into tiny droplets that enter the lacteal and travel in the lymph before joining the blood.
asks: Where do fats go after digestion?

faq.q: How long is the small intestine?
faq.a: In an adult it is roughly 6 to 7 metres long, coiled up in the belly. It is called small because it is narrow, not because it is short.
asks: Why is it called the small intestine?

facts: Villi are about 0.5 to 1 millimetre tall.
The adult small intestine is roughly 6 to 7 metres long.
Digested fats enter lacteals, lymph vessels inside the villi, rather than going straight into the blood.

quiz.say: Why does the small intestine have villi and microvilli?
quiz.show: Why does the small intestine have villi and microvilli?

options.show: To make a much bigger surface for absorbing food
options.say: To make a much bigger surface for absorbing food

quiz.why: More surface means more nutrients can pass into the blood at once.

wrong.1: Villi do not change the length; they add surface inside.
wrong.2: The intestine absorbs food; it does not store it there.
